fields.name: data_type
fields.documentation: The element type of this value's bytes when they are a plain array -- the ONE place it lives (a sampled_body never repeats it). Needed only when the bytes are a plain array the schema does not type: a `sampled_body`, or an untyped inline array (rule `data_type_when_bytes`). Bytes in an `opaque_body` need none: its `format` term is the encoding (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21). `datum_type` until 2026-10-08, renamed once the class `data_type` became `value`; it is the v1 spelling of the same fact (binaryseries_parameters, ngrid, ...).

fields.name: source_data_type
fields.documentation: The source's own spelling, OMITTED when it is already canonical. Kept because the map is NOT invertible -- `bool` maps back to `logical` OR `ubit1`, and `char` has no canonical at all -- so retaining it makes the normalisation AUDITABLE: the corpus can be queried afterwards to verify every `float64` came from a `double` rather than from a default.

fields.name: data_body
fields.documentation: True: this value's bytes are in data_body documents that point here through `owner_id`. False (the default): the value is inline in `value`. Never neither (rule `value_inline_or_body`): a value with no inline `value` must say `data_body: true`. A document marked true with no body pointing at it has lost its data -- the batch check (item 60).

rules.name: data_type_when_bytes
rules.statement: `data_type` is required only when the value's bytes are a plain array: in a `sampled_body`, or an untyped inline value (a bare numeric or text array, not a declared cell). When its bodies are opaque (`opaque_body`), their `format` term is the encoding and no `data_type` is needed; a typed cell already says its type (`temperature.value.celsius` is a double). A body's kind is not visible on the owner, so the sampled_body half is a batch check. (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21; did_v2_data_body_model_plan.md AMENDMENT 5.)

rules.name: value_inline_or_body
rules.statement: A value is inline (its `value` field filled) or in data bodies (`data_body` true), never neither; a statement may instead take its value from a shared value document through a non-empty `value_id` edge (statement.json), which is itself inline or in bodies. This one rule replaces a per-class required `value` (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21, signed: did_v2_data_body_model_plan.md AMENDMENT 5 and its clarification). A blank `value` is also accepted when the run's migration report lists it, or a field within it (`<block>.value...`), as a gap of the document: a fact the source never stated, such as a formulation in which no ingredient states an amount (Jess Haley, 2026-10-31, did_v2_go_forward_class_audit.md [formulation amount needs info]; listed in the report, not the document, since [gap accepted when the report lists it], 2026-11-01).
